grh_e593afafbae6b0b0d761.title: Remember the Night
paragraphs: Lee Leander is arrested for stealing a diamond bracelet just before Christmas, and prosecutor John Sargent has the case postponed until after the holidays rather than risk a sympathetic jury. Feeling responsible for leaving her jailed over Christmas, John arranges bail and discovers that Lee has nowhere worth returning to, so he takes her along to his own family home. The warmth of Johnâ€™s mother and aunt gives Lee a glimpse of the honest life she never had, and she and John fall in love on the trip back to New York. At trial John quietly tries to give her every possible chance, but Lee refuses to let his love compromise his duty. She pleads guilty, accepting that she must pay for what she did. John promises to stand beside her through sentencing and whatever prison term follows, while Lee hopes that if he still wants her afterward they can begin together on equal terms.

grh_e54495a1fdc144672aca.title: Silver Annie
paragraphs: Virtue City is dying, and railroad men need a right-of-way through the old Huxley mine, but stubborn Annie Huxley refuses to give up property she still believes contains silver. Her relatives use her behavior and a shooting incident to try to have her declared incompetent. Britt has ore from the mine assayed and produces a rich result at the hearing, making Annie's belief look reasonable enough to stop the commitment. Annie privately reveals that Britt used old ore from the mine's original strike, but the excitement sends prospectors back into the district and soon leads to a genuine new silver discovery.
